method: A stained-glass panel is bought as flat glass, came or foil and solder, and this page turns the piece list into those four quantities. Glass area is width times height for every piece, multiplied by its count and added up. The came length follows from the seams: every piece has a perimeter, an inside edge is shared by exactly two pieces, and the panel border is an edge of one piece only. Summing the perimeters therefore counts each inside seam twice and the border once, so the came length is half the sum of the perimeters plus the panel perimeter; for a 12 by 16 inch panel cut into four pieces with perimeters 40, 24, 32 and 16 inches, that is (112 + 56) / 2 = 84 inches. Copper foil is a strip wrapped around every edge of every piece, so it is the sum of the perimeters, and solder runs down both faces of every seam, so its length is the sum of the perimeters plus the panel perimeter; a single-piece panel is the check case, where came equals the border, foil equals the border and solder equals twice the border. Glass coverage is the glass area divided by the panel area and is shown as a percentage, so a piece list that does not fit the panel is visible at once. The estimate assumes the pieces tile the panel edge to edge with no gaps or overlaps, and it is a buying figure: it makes no allowance for cutting waste, so order a little more glass, and the size each piece is cut to still comes from the pattern, because bevels, textured glass and the heart width of the came all move the cut line. Dimensions are read in inches or centimetres, the two systems are converted with the exact 2.54 cm inch rather than a rounded factor, counts are whole numbers from 1 to 200, and results are rounded to two decimals. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
